prompt:
Each of your ideas must draw on a domain unrelated to the research question below, for example through an analogy, a structure, a principle, or a pattern borrowed from that domain, while still being a concrete, scientifically sound way to address the question.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Magnetic hysteresis loop for AP-1 dose-response
ideas.description: Borrowing from ferromagnetic hysteresis, expose cells to a ramped-up then ramped-down stimulus (e.g., optogenetic or chemically controlled FOS/JUN input) and measure AP-1 occupancy (CUT&RUN) and target gene expression along both paths. A non-overlapping loop, with residual signal at zero stimulus, would indicate path-dependent memory attributable to AP-1.

ideas.title: Immunological recall-response analogy: prime-challenge-rechallenge with AP-1 degron
ideas.description: Like vaccine prime/boost designs, give cells a first stimulus, rest them for variable intervals, then re-stimulate, measuring faster or stronger transcription at primed loci by nascent RNA-seq (PRO-seq). Acutely degrading (dTAG) AP-1 factors only during priming versus only during recall separates AP-1's role in establishing versus retrieving memory.

ideas.title: Neuronal engram-style lineage tracing of AP-1 history
ideas.description: Inspired by activity-dependent engram labeling (e.g., FOS-driven TRAP), use an AP-1-driven Cre or recorder to permanently tag cells that experienced AP-1 activation, then compare tagged and untagged sibling cells for later chromatin accessibility (scATAC) and response to re-stimulation. This tests whether past AP-1 activity predicts durable, cell-autonomous state differences.

ideas.title: Kinetic proofreading / persistence-time modeling from single-cell live imaging
ideas.description: Borrowing the signal-processing concept of memory kernels from physics and control theory, image endogenously tagged FOS/JUN and a transcription reporter in single cells over days, then fit autocorrelation and mutual-information decay times. Compare decay times with AP-1 protein half-life and chromatin mark half-life to see if persistence exceeds what protein turnover alone explains.

ideas.title: Epigenetic 'pioneer footprint' test using ecological succession logic
ideas.description: As in ecological succession, where early colonizers modify the habitat for later species, test whether AP-1 opens enhancers that remain accessible after AP-1 is removed. Perform time-course ATAC-seq, H3K27ac ChIP and motif analysis after stimulus withdrawal, and use dCas9-based tethering of AP-1 or motif mutation at selected enhancers to test if accessibility persistence is AP-1-dependent and sufficient to enhance later responses.
